column11: Meet Dragon  a handsome 3-year-old Doberman with a big playful heart!Dragon is a really good boy who loves his people and thrives on affection and attention. He does great with people and dogs once he knows them  and he currently has other foster dog friends that he plays with on a regular basis but can be selective of others.Dragon can just be weary of strangers at first  so he does best with slow introductions to new people and new animals to set him up for success. He is currently on Prozac to help him feel more settled and confident  and he is doing well on it.He'll be happiest with an experienced handler who understands the breed  can read his cues  and can continue his routine. In return  you'll get a loyal  goofy  intelligent and affectionate best friend who loves toys  car rides  and an active lifestyle.Dragon is housetrained  crate trained  and neutered. He needs a home with a fenced yard  no cats  and older/considerate kids only.If you're looking for a fun  loving companion and can give him a little patience up front with new faces  Dragon might be your perfect match!

Meet Doberman puppy Onyx!  Onyx is a 11-month-old melanistic Doberman puppy with a gentle soul and a powerful comeback story. He and his brother Bonsai were found as strays and came into rescue in rough shape—both boys were very skinny  one required stitches  and the other was running a fever. All healthy now and fully vetted  vaccinated and neutered  he is ready to find his forever home! Thanks to prompt veterinary care  good nutrition  and lots of love  both pups have made an amazing recovery and are now doing great! Onyx is dog friendly and does well around other pups. . Like any puppy his age  Onyx is curious  learning about the world  and ready to bond deeply with his people. He’s at the perfect stage of life to grow  train  and build confidence alongside a committed forever family. Onyx has already proven how resilient he is—now he’s ready for a safe  loving forever home where he can continue to thrive. If you’re looking for a pup to grow with and love for a lifetime  Onyx might be your perfect match. www.uniteddobermanrescue.org

Meet 1 year old  cropped docked purebred Doberman Tootsie. Tootsie is a barely 1-year-old young Doberman girl whose story is one of survival  resilience  and the slow  brave journey back to trust.She is cropped and docked  and still just a baby—yet she has already endured more than most dogs ever should.Tootsie was picked up in California and spent over two long months in a Los Angeles shelter—surrounded by constant noise  barking 24/7  and overwhelming chaos. For a sensitive breed like a Doberman  that environment can be devastating. Tootsie completely shut down. She stopped responding to people  retreating into herself just to cope.Every small step forward is a victory. We are also learning more about her personality as she decompresses. Tootsie finds comfort in her crate and will often seek it out as her safe space—it’s where she feels most secure. She is fully potty trained  but in true “safe-zone” fashion  she may choose to settle in her crate for long stretches and will sometimes need gentle encouragement to come out and engage with the world around her. For her  the crate is not a problem—it’s her refuge.Right now  Tootsie is building confidence. She will need a fenced yard and humans who can be super patient with her healing and bonding journey. She came so close to losing her life  and she deserves the chance to truly live it. Tootsie is fully vetted and spayed.We won’t give up on Tootsie—and one day  she will have a family to call her own. Tootsie will need a high fenced yard and gps collar as she is a serious flight risk. Sudden noises like a car honk  siren  bangs send her into a tailspin of fear. She also prefers the company of other dogs so a home with other canines is a must. Her best pal right now is a tiny Yorkie!  Please read our adoption policy and if you qualify  please apply at: www.uniteddobermanrescue.org

MEET MAGGIE  THE BLUE BEAUTY WITH A BIG PERSONALITY! 5-year-old blue purebred Doberman. Dog-friendly. Fabulous. Absolutely  positively NO CATS.This stunning blue Doberman Pinscher has entered the building  and she would like everyone to know that she is fabulous. Maggie is beautiful  sweet  loyal  and equipped with just the right amount of Doberman sass. She has a big heart  a fun personality  and absolutely no intention of being a wallflower.Through no fault of her own  changes in her family's circumstances meant Maggie lost the home she knew. Now this gorgeous girl is ready to turn the page and find the people who will make her next chapter her forever chapter.Her resume:✨ Blue and beautiful. Yes  she knows.✨ Sweet and loyal. Once you're her person  you're her person.✨ Sass level: just right. Not too much  not too little. Doberman standard.✨ Easy to get along with. A real people-pleaser  unless there's a snack involved  in which case she'd like to discuss this development.And Maggie has exciting news... SHE LIKES DOGS! She loves having other dogs around and would be happy to share her humans  her toys  her adventures  and probably her opinions with a compatible four-legged roommate.Now  the kitty question.   Maggie's answer is a firm no. Maggie has a high prey drive for little critters  and she is not a fan of cats. It's not personal  it's just who she is. Her forever home needs to be cat-free. No cats  no way  no exceptions  no "but he's really friendly." Please don't ask. Maggie has made up her mind  and she's a Doberman  so she's not changing it.What Maggie wants in her people:This girl is ready for FUN! She wants a family who will include her in life  give her stability and structure  and let her be the silly  loving  slightly sassy Doberman she was born to be.Maggie is not looking for a temporary pit stop. She is looking for HER PEOPLE. The kind of people who will say  "Yes  Maggie  you may come with us." Going for a walk? Maggie's coming. Adventure? Maggie's coming. Road trip? Maggie is already in the car.️ Couch time? Obviously Maggie is coming. Someone has a snack? Maggie would like to discuss this development.She is a loyal companion with an enormous heart  and once she knows you are her people  you can expect plenty of Doberman devotion.Maggie is fully ready to leave her past behind and get busy living her best life. She has beauty  brains  personality  and dog-friendliness. All she needs is the forever family who sees what a special girl she is.Maggie is blue. Maggie is beautiful.Maggie is dog-friendly.Maggie is NOT cat-friendly  and that's okay.Maggie has Doberman sass.Maggie has a giant heart.And Maggie is READY to be someone's best friend!Think your home might be Maggie's happily-ever-after? Apply to adopt this gorgeous girl today! United Doberman Rescue | www.uniteddobermanrescue.org

Meet purebred Doberman Vinny! Meet Vinny  a handsome 6-7 year-old black and rust purebred Doberman Pinscher! Vinny is a true gentleman who has been there  done that  and is ready to find a loving family to call his own.Due to changes in his family’s circumstances  Vinny is looking for a fresh start and a new forever home. Through no fault of his own  he has lost the home he knew and is now ready for a new chapter with a family who will give him the love  patience  and stability he deserves.Vinny is a loyal  devoted boy with a soft heart and plenty of personality. He’s the kind of dog who forms deep connections with his people and loves being close to those he trusts. Whether he’s relaxing by your side or soaking up some attention  Vinny is happiest when he’s with his humans. Check him out playing with other dogs: https://www.facebook.com/reel/4482537615294038After everything he’s been through  Vinny deserves a family who will show him just how wonderful life can be. If you’re looking for a mature  loyal Doberman gentleman with a heart of gold  Vinny may be the perfect match for you!If you’re ready to give Vinny the forever home he deserves  apply today to adopt!www.uniteddobermanrescue.org

ATLAS... PART-TIME GOOBER  FULL-TIME DOBERMAN SECURITY DETAIL We have a bit of a naming crisis on our hands. We are torn between calling him Atlas  because apparently his compass is full and he's trying to figure out which direction his life is supposed to go... Or Doby  because "Doby" sounds suspiciously like the name you give a dog who has entered the Witness Protection Program and is not at liberty to discuss his previous life. ️‍♂️And honestly  we're starting to think Doby has been instructed by his attorney to say nothing without his human present.Because here's what we know: This 1-year-old Doberman arrived with very little information and approximately 17 000 unanswered questions. He was dropped off at a foster's boarding facility without official approval  with almost no history. We were told he had lived with children  another dog  and that his name was Doby.That's it. Apparently  the rest of his biography was classified.When he first arrived  he was scared  confused and understandably unsure about what was happening. But once he started settling in  we discovered something important:THIS BOY IS A TOTAL DOG NUT.LOVES other dogs.Playing? YES.Romping? YES.Wrestling? ABSOLUTELY.Running around like someone just announced free pizza? EVERY SINGLE TIME.He has been having a blast at daycare and absolutely LOVES hanging out with his canine friends.Give him another dog and suddenly the worried  uncertain boy disappears and the Doberman version of a professional WWE wrestler comes out.But then there's the other side of this handsome guy.He's a Doberman.And apparently his internal software came with the "Protect My People at All Costs" package pre-installed.Once he bonds with his humans  he is going to love them HARD. He will want to be with his people  know where his people are and keep tabs on his people.Strangers?Well...Strangers may apply for access. He will probably want to personally review their credentials  references  employment history and possibly their intentions regarding the snack cabinet.This is why Atlas/Doby is NOT a first-time Doberman.He needs someone who already understands this breed and knows that a Doberman can be loving  goofy  affectionate  intelligent  loyal and protective......sometimes all before breakfast.He is young and still needs refinement. He needs continued training  structure  consistency and someone who will help him learn that he doesn't have to worry about everything going on around him.And let's be clear:He WANTS to learn.He's young. He's smart. He's curious. He's playful. He's figuring things out.He's not looking for someone who expects a perfectly finished product.He's looking for someone who looks at him and says:"Yep. I know Dobermans. I got this."Because when he decides you're his person  you're probably going to know about it.❤️ You will be loved.️ You will be protected.You will be monitored.You will probably be followed into the bathroom. And heaven help the suspicious-looking Amazon delivery driver.Because of his fear and uncertainty  a secure physical fence is non-negotiable. We require a tall privacy fence or very tall chain-link fence. No invisible fences  tie-outs or unfenced properties.He has previously lived with children ages 1 through 9 and two other dogs  a little Yorkie and a large Lab. We're told those dogs apparently had him thoroughly trained in the art of knowing his place. Now he's discovering that life can actually be pretty fantastic.He gets to play with dogs. He gets to wrestle. He gets to romp. He gets to make friends.And slowly  he's learning that people can be trusted too.What Atlas/Doby needs now is his person. Not just anybody.Not someone who thinks  "I've never owned a Doberman  but how hard could it be?"Nope. We're looking for an experienced Doberman owner who understands the breed  understands protective behavior  enjoys training and is willing to help this young guy grow into the confident  well-mannered Doberman he's capable of becoming.He isn't perfect. He's not supposed to be. He's one year old.He's a work in progress with a giant heart  a goofy personality  a serious dog-playing addiction and a security system that apparently cannot be turned off.Underneath the uncertainty is a very special dog waiting for someone who will take the time to earn his trust.He may steal your heart. He may steal your couch. He may steal your personal space.And there is a very good chance he will steal your other dog's dignity during a wrestling match. ❤️He just needs someone willing to help him figure out where he belongs.Which brings us right back to the name...Atlas? Because his compass is full.Doby? Because apparently he's in Witness Protection. ️‍♂️We're taking votes.Whatever we eventually call him  this boy is ready for a new chapter  preferably one involving good people  good dogs  plenty of wrestling and absolutely no more mysterious plot twists.❤️ United Doberman Rescue www.uniteddobermanrescue.org

2-year-old Dober-girl  Jessie was sitting in a shelter  waiting for the grim reaper to call her number. That day was only days away. Thankfully  United Doberman Rescue (UDR) stepped in  tagged her for safety in our rescue  and gave her the second chance she so desperately deserved. Jessie was welcomed into an amazing  loving foster home where she has received all of the veterinary care she should have had long ago. Spayed  vaccinated  heartworm checked and chipped. Now  she's almost ready to begin the next chapter of her life—with a family of her own.Jessie is truly a gentle  sweet Doberman whose only wish is to love and be loved. She does wonderfully with other dogs and has enjoyed being part of her foster family. Whether she's spending time with her canine companions or soaking up affection from her people  Jessie is simply happiest being included and loved.We will never understand how a Doberman with such a wonderful temperament ended up in an overcrowded shelter where healthy  loving dogs lose their lives simply because there wasn't enough space. Those days are behind her now. Jessie is safe  cherished  and now will be searching for the forever family she has always deserved.If you open your heart to Jessie  she promises to fill your home with unwavering loyalty  unconditional love  and the special devotion that only a Doberman can give. Every day  her gratitude will shine through in the way she looks at you  leans into you  and loves you with her whole heart. The lucky person who adopts Jessie won't just be saving a dog—they'll be gaining a best friend for years to come.Jessie's story is  unfortunately  the story of far too many Dobermans. But thanks to the angels who helped guide her to United Doberman Rescue  her story now has the chance for a happy ending. Could you be the one to give her that ending?If you think Jessie could be the missing piece of your family  visit www.uniteddobermanrescue.org and complete an adoption application if you qualify.Jessie is no longer waiting for her life to end—she's waiting for someone to show her that her best days are still ahead. ❤️

Meet Diamond! Diamond is a beautiful purebred blue Dober-girl somewhere between 1 and 2 years old  with a youthful  goofy spirit that makes her seem even younger. She is smart  playful  curious  and has the kind of personality that makes you smile just watching her figure out the world.Diamond spent nearly a year at a boarding facility in California  so she is now discovering that the world is a MUCH bigger place than a kennel. New people? Interesting. New experiences? Hmmm... let's investigate. Weird things she has never seen before? She is working on it! The wonderful thing about Diamond is that she really tries to be the best girl. She wants to do the right thing  and you can almost see the wheels turning as she learns about all these new things she may not have experienced while living at the kennel. Give her a little patience  encouragement  and guidance  and she is eager to figure it out.It is also VERY apparent that Diamond has had some serious obedience training. She knows her commands and clearly understands what is expected of her. She sits when its leash time  sits when the door opens and waits for you to tell her to go through. We suspect she may have spent some time as a board-and-train at the kennel she was at because this girl has some impressive skills!She loves going for walks and is a fantastic car passenger. Diamond is quite happy riding shotgun  taking in the scenery and making sure everyone is following proper driving procedures. And then there is the ball. Diamond LOVES to play ball. Throw it  she is on it. Throw it again  she is ready. And again. And again. We are pretty sure she would happily make ball retrieval her full-time career if someone would just keep the paycheck coming in tennis balls. Diamond is dog-friendly. Once she feels comfortable with humans  her playful personality comes out. She is affectionate  curious  and wants to be involved in whatever her people are doing.She isn't normally much of a talker  but put her in a crate and suddenly she has a LOT to say. Apparently  Diamond believes being crated is the perfect time to provide everyone within earshot with her thoughts on the situation. She is also learning about some of the stranger things that come with being a house dog. The robot vacuum  or computer printer  for example  neither has not exactly won her endorsement. She is still reviewing those particular pieces of technology. She clearly does not approve.Diamond is such a fun combination of youthful energy  intelligence  sweetness  and personality. She is learning every day  and watching her gain confidence as she experiences new things is pretty special. She would love a family who will continue her training  give her plenty of exercise and mental stimulation  play lots of ball  take her on adventures  and help her learn that all those new and sometimes weird things in the world are actually okay. Diamond tends to be very clingy once she determines you are her person.She does startle easily by new things so a fully fenced yard will be required. Clearly learning about the outside world in her foster home.Diamond is fully vetted  spayed  microchipped  current on vaccinations  heartworm negative  and on preventative. She is ready to keep learning  keep playing  and most importantly  finally have a family of her own. Diamond is fostered in Arizona. Adopters will need to travel to meet and adopt. Learn more about Diamond and adopting with United Doberman Rescue at www.uniteddobermanrescue.org

Meet baby Blair!Blair’s name means “plain” or “field ” which feels almost too fitting for this sweet girl considering the journey that brought her to us. Blair was found abandoned all alone in a field in Iowa  and despite such a rough start  she has remained nothing but a happy and loving puppy.We estimated Blair’s birthday based on the amount of puppy teeth she had when she was found—she barely had any! She was clearly just a tiny baby when she was left to fend for herself  but you would never know it from her personality.Blair is a happy-go-lucky  HIGH-energy breed puppy who is ready to find a family that can keep up with her! She will thrive with an active family who wants a fun-loving adventure buddy and is ready to give her plenty of exercise  enrichment  training  and  of course  snuggles.She is great with other dogs AND cats  making her a wonderful addition to a multi-pet home. We also think she would be an amazing fit for a family with kids who can keep her busy—because Blair will happily return the favor and keep them busy too! Talk about a win-win!This girl is sweet  silly  playful  energetic  and ready to put her past behind her and start the next chapter of her life. After everything she has been through  Blair deserves a family who will show her just how wonderful life can be.Beyond her playful energy  Blair is incredibly smart and has already mastered "sit" and is a total pro at playing fetch. She’s highly food and treat-motivated  which makes her training an absolute breeze and shows how eager she is to learn. She'll do best with a playful canine companion who can keep up with her high-energy lifestyle.If you’re looking for a fun  active  affectionate puppy who will bring plenty of personality and adventure into your life  Blair might just be your girl!https://www.uniteddobermanrescue.org/

Meet Penny!Penny is a sweet young girl who we estimate to be around 6 months old  and she has already been through more than any puppy should have to endure. Penny came to us from Animal Control in Wisconsin after suffering a severe broken leg. Despite everything she has been through  this little girl continues to show us just how resilient and loving she is.Penny’s leg may ultimately need to be amputated  but because she is still so young  we are confident that she will adapt incredibly well if that ends up being the best option for her. We will be working closely with our veterinary team and following their recommendations to make sure Penny receives whatever care is truly in her best interest.Right now  Penny is focused on being a puppy — learning  growing  and soaking up all the love she deserves. She is looking for a family who understands that she may have some extra medical needs along the way  but who also sees what we see: a bright  beautiful little girl with so much life ahead of her.Penny has already overcome so much in her short life  and we cannot wait to see what her future holds. She deserves a family who will give her patience  love  and the chance to show everyone just how special she is.Penny may have had a rough start  but we know her best days are still ahead.

Meet Logan ❤️ Logan is a handsome 1-year-old purebred  neutered  Doberman who is ready to trade his shelter days for the good life he deserves. This young guy found himself in a shelter  but thankfully  his story didn’t end there. United Doberman Rescue stepped in  and now Logan is looking forward to finding his forever family.One of Logan’s favorite things in the whole world? OTHER FEMALE DOGS! He genuinely enjoys canine company and loves having a four-legged friend around to play  romp  and share life with. His playful personality is still very much that of a young Doberman  so his forever family should be ready for the energy  enthusiasm  and occasional “I have absolutely no idea what my legs are doing” moments that come with a young Dober-boy.At just one year old  Logan is still growing into himself. He will need continued training  structure  exercise  and guidance to help him become the confident  well-mannered adult Doberman he is meant to be. He would thrive with an active family who understands that young Dobermans are not decorative furniture. They need things to do  places to go  and humans willing to help them learn how to be excellent members of the household. Logan also need extra groceries on his skinny Doberman body!Adoption Requirements and UDR policies:• A securely fenced yard is preferred.• An active household that can provide daily exercise  training  mental stimulation  and plenty of family time.• Another compatible female dog in the home would be a wonderful bonus  since Logan genuinely enjoys canine companionship.• Adopters should understand the Doberman breed and be prepared for the energy  intelligence  sensitivity  and Velcro tendencies that come with it.• Continued obedience training and positive reinforcement are expected as Logan grows into adulthood.• Logan must be an indoor family dog. Dobermans belong with their people  not living outside in the backyard.• All current pets must be up to date on veterinary care and appropriate preventatives.• A home visit and veterinary reference check are required before adoption.• Logan must be adopted within the United States. UDR does not ship or transport dogs internationally.• Adoption is not first-come  first-served. Our goal is to find the home that is the best fit for Logan and the family adopting him.Logan may have started his journey in a shelter  but his future can be so much bigger. His bags are packed. His Doberman heart is ready. Now he just needs his people. Could you be Logan’s forever family?Learn more about Logan and United Doberman Rescue:www.uniteddobermanrescue.org

Meet Klaus! Handsome doesn't begin to cover it. This sweet  approximately 3½-year-old neutered Doberman is a gentle soul with a heart as big as his ears are perky  and he's ready to find the family he's been dreaming about.Klaus loves people of all ages  and he's a total pro with kids. He even has a 4-year-old human buddy who thinks he hung the moon. He's equally smooth with other dogs  getting along with both boys and girls  though he'd really love a female canine companion to share the couch with. Fair warning: Klaus is not a fan of cats  so his forever home needs to be cat-free.Klaus is a smart cookie  too. He knows his basic commands and has an excellent recall  so when you call  he comes running (probably with a goofy grin). He's never possessive of his food or toys  and he is affectionate to the core  the kind of dog who will happily lean into you for one more cuddle.He's up to date on his vaccinations and is currently being treated for allergies. Like any good student  Klaus has one subject he's still working on: leash walking. With a little patience  structure  and continued training  he'll be strutting down the sidewalk like a champ.Klaus has so much love to give. All he needs is a family who will offer patience  guidance  and most of all  a permanent place to call home. Could that be you?Learn more about adopting Klaus at https://www.uniteddobermanrescue.org/

Meet Brandy  a stunning 5-year-old AKC red Doberman beauty who is every bit as sweet as she is beautiful!Brandy has spent nearly her entire life devoted to one person. Since she was just 10 weeks old  she lived with her elderly human as his companion  and in true Doberman fashion  she took that job very seriously. Unfortunately  her owner recently had to move into assisted living  and his family made the difficult decision to find Brandy a new home where she can receive all the love  attention  and companionship she deserves.Brandy is a typical Dobe when it comes to her home and her person. She bonds closely with her human and will absolutely let strangers know she is there when they enter her territory. Once she knows you  though  you'll quickly see the sweet girl behind that beautiful red exterior.Because Brandy has not lived with any other pets since she was a very young puppy  we simply don't know yet how she feels about sharing her life with other animals. Any introductions to dogs or other pets should be done slowly  correctly  and with plenty of time for everyone to become comfortable. She shouldn't be rushed into interactions just because she hasn't shown us yet what her preferences are.Brandy has spent the last five years being someone's loyal companion  and now she's looking for someone who will be hers. She deserves a home that understands the devotion  intelligence  and protective nature that comes with loving a Doberman—and  most importantly  a family ready to make her part of their world again.This red beauty has so much love and loyalty left to give. Could Brandy be your girl?

Meet Rufio! Rufio is a stunning 10-month-old Doberman who is ready to find his forever home! This handsome young guy is dog friendly and super smart  making him highly trainable and eager to learn. He has plenty of typical young Doberman energy and will thrive with an active family who enjoys training  exercise  and giving their dog plenty of appropriate outlets. Rufio has lived with cats and can coexist with them  but he does enjoy chasing and trying to play with them  so a home without cats may be the best fit. Rufio is a strong  energetic young Doberman who will do best with an experienced  confident handler who can provide structure  consistency  and continued training. He is NOT a good fit for a home with kids. With the right guidance  this smart boy has the potential to be an amazing companion! Rufio will be neutered as soon as possible as part of his adoption process. If you're looking for a smart  energetic  trainable young Doberman to grow and learn with  Rufio may be your guy! https://www.uniteddobermanrescue.org/

column11: Meet Scooby!Scooby is a big  handsome guy estimated to be around 5 years old and weighing in at approximately 86 pounds! This California stray recently found himself on the euthanasia list  but thankfully  his story isn't ending there. Scooby has been given a second chance and is preparing to begin his next chapter in foster care with United Doberman Rescue & Canine Castaways.The shelter reports that Scooby appears to be dog friendly  although he struggled in the shelter environment. Shelters can be stressful and overwhelming  so we're looking forward to seeing how Scooby settles into a home and learning more about his personality  preferences  and needs.As Scooby decompresses in foster care  we'll continue getting to know him and sharing updates about what makes him special and what kind of forever home will help him thrive.For now  Scooby is a big guy with a second chance at the life he deserves. Stay tuned as we learn more about this handsome newcomer!Interested in giving Scooby his forever home? Visit our website to learn more about our adoption process and submit an application. Fostered in Californiahttps://www.uniteddobermanrescue.org/
